boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented UNH traditions, mixing current Wildcat rituals with clearly labeled historical practices preserved by UNH Libraries.

cards.title: Pat the Cat
cards.subtitle: Wildcat statue, UNH Durham campus
cards.notes: Stop by the Wildcat statue and rub its nose for good luck; UNH admissions describes the ritual as spanning campus tours through graduation.
cards.short_summary: A current good-luck ritual centered on UNH’s Wildcat statue.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH Admissions documents “pat the cat” as rubbing the Wildcat statue’s nose for good luck throughout a student’s UNH journey.
cards.access_notes: The source identifies the Wildcat statue as the setting; check campus access conditions before visiting.

cards.title: Fish on the Ice
cards.subtitle: UNH hockey at the Whittemore Center
cards.notes: Watch for the first UNH hockey goal: the university’s visitor guide identifies fish on the ice as the signal that the Wildcats have scored.
cards.short_summary: A hockey-goal tradition with an unmistakably fishy visual cue.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH’s Whittemore Center tour states that fish on the ice means UNH hockey scored its first goal.
cards.source_title: Whittemore Center | Explore the University of New Hampshire
cards.access_notes: Observe venue and event rules; this card documents the tradition and does not instruct visitors to throw objects.

cards.title: The Freshman Beanie Era
cards.subtitle: Historical UNH tradition — ended with the Class of 1971
cards.notes: See the archive record of blue freshman caps with white buttons, once used to identify newcomers and build class spirit.
cards.short_summary: A long-running freshman identifier, now a documented archive tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH’s museum says freshman beanies began in 1909 and that the Class of 1971 was the last required to wear one.
cards.source_title: Out of the Cat's Closet: The University Museum's Unique Collection
cards.access_notes: Historical and discontinued; view the university archive material rather than attempting to revive a requirement.

cards.title: Carry a Senior Cane
cards.subtitle: Historical UNH graduation custom — replaced in 1940
cards.notes: Explore the archival images of seniors carrying canes in their final weeks, often marked by classmates as personal mementos.
cards.short_summary: Graduation-era walking canes preceded UNH’s senior-ring custom.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH Libraries records that senior canes symbolized impending graduation and were replaced with a senior ring in 1940.
cards.source_title: Out of the Cat's Closet: The University Museum's Unique Collection
cards.access_notes: Historical and discontinued; the source includes an archival photograph of seniors with a class cane.

cards.title: The Main Street Rules Posters
cards.subtitle: Historical UNH custom along Main Street
cards.notes: Read the archive’s account of sophomores posting first-year rules overnight along Main Street before the start of classes.
cards.short_summary: A former class-rivalry ritual documented by UNH’s museum.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH Libraries documents that sophomores wrote and posted Freshman Rules posters along Main Street for freshmen to remove or obey.
cards.source_title: Out of the Cat's Closet: The University Museum's Unique Collection
cards.access_notes: Historical only; do not post materials on campus property or recreate class-enforcement practices.

cards.title: Build the Field on New Hampshire Day
cards.subtitle: Historical campus workday — 1916 to 1924
cards.notes: Trace the 1916 campus-wide workday when classes paused and students and faculty improved what is now Memorial Field.
cards.short_summary: A former all-campus labor day devoted to the athletic field.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH Libraries states that the first New Hampshire Day was held in 1916 and the annual event continued until 1924.
cards.source_title: The Way We Were: A Collection of UNH Anecdotes
cards.access_notes: Historical and discontinued; use the archive exhibit to learn about the event.

cards.title: Elect a “Mayor” of Durham
cards.subtitle: Historical Homecoming tradition — 1926 through the 1960s
cards.notes: Follow the archive account of student mayoral campaigns, voting under Thompson Hall’s arch, and a Homecoming-game ceremonial winner.
cards.short_summary: A former student election that turned Homecoming into mock civic theater.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH Libraries says Mayor of Durham campaigns began in 1926, continued into the 1960s, and the winner appeared at the Homecoming football game.
cards.source_title: Bulls, Wildcats & Mayors: Sports & Social Traditions
cards.access_notes: Historical and discontinued; Thompson Hall is referenced as the former voting location.

cards.title: Winter Carnival’s Ski-Jump Origins
cards.subtitle: Historical UNH winter-sports tradition — begun in 1922
cards.notes: Use the museum exhibit to follow the Forestry Club’s first carnival, then the Outing Club’s expanded winter games and carnival ball.
cards.short_summary: UNH’s early winter festival combined outdoor competition and social events.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH Libraries documents the first Winter Carnival in 1922 and its later Outing Club sponsorship with winter sports and snow-related games.
cards.source_title: Bulls, Wildcats & Mayors: Sports & Social Traditions
cards.access_notes: Historical exhibit material; the source describes the original locations and activities.

cards.title: Casque and Casket’s Spring Dance
cards.subtitle: Historical inter-fraternity event — formed in 1905
cards.notes: Read the archival description of this senior-junior society’s annual spring dance and its theatrical opening procession with a casket.
cards.short_summary: A notably theatrical former spring social event preserved in UNH archives.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH Libraries identifies Casque and Casket as an inter-fraternity senior-junior society formed in 1905 and describes its annual spring dance.
cards.source_title: The Way We Were: A Collection of UNH Anecdotes
cards.access_notes: Historical only; the source is an archive exhibit describing the former event.

cards.entity_name: Wildcat Marching Band AlumniBand at Homecoming
cards.title: Bring AlumniBand Back for Homecoming
cards.subtitle: Wildcat Marching Band tradition at UNH Homecoming
cards.notes: Look for the Wildcat Marching Band’s AlumniBand at Homecoming, one of the traditions listed in the band’s official handbook.
cards.short_summary: A band-community Homecoming tradition that reconnects alumni performers.
cards.evidence_claim: The UNH Wildcat Marching Band handbook lists hosting AlumniBand at Homecoming among the organization’s continuing traditions.
cards.access_notes: Confirm current Homecoming and band-event details with UNH before attending.
